theme: Protect income. Care for home. Build our way forward.
northStar: Keep work, family time, home responsibilities, and our longer-term transition visible in one place so neither of us has to reconstruct the plan from scattered calendars and chats.
workNorthStar: Protect dependable income while replacing lower-leverage hours with better work and repeatable 3DVR revenue, without letting the business consume home and family life.
operatingRule: Home and family count as real work. Protect booked income, protect recovery time, take care of the house, then use the best open blocks for higher-leverage work.
workOperatingRule: Work → earn → follow up → stabilize → ship. Revenue and reliability come before feature sprawl, while home/family blocks stay protected.

sharedFocus.title: Mexico house care window
sharedFocus.detail: Protect this as real household time before the next dense work run. Handle the important maintenance first, keep some family/rest time, and leave Tuesday with enough buffer to reset.
checklist: Make one short house-maintenance list before leaving
Prioritize safety, moisture, utilities, cleaning, and anything getting worse
Keep at least one half-day unstructured for family/rest
Return Tuesday with Wednesday morning protected for reset

items.title: Tonight — keep it light
items.sharedDetail: No second full shift tonight. Organize, decompress, and keep the evening usable for home/family.
items.detail: Keep implementation light. Small cleanup is fine; avoid turning tonight into another founder shift.

items.title: Work day
items.sharedDetail: Booked work day. Evening should stay mostly free unless something truly urgent comes up.
items.detail: Protect booked income and let automation handle routine business activity around the shift.

items.title: Work day
items.sharedDetail: Work until 4 PM. Keep the rest of Sunday simple and recover for the early Monday start.
items.detail: Treat this as an earn-and-recover day; business systems can keep leads and documentation moving quietly.

items.title: Morning work + useful afternoon
items.sharedDetail: Work ends at noon. Use part of the afternoon for important admin, but keep enough energy for home life.
items.detail: After work, prioritize active paid work, strong applications, client pipeline, then portal reliability.

items.title: Long workday
items.sharedDetail: Treat this as a work-and-recover day. No expectation of a big 3DVR push afterward.
items.detail: Keep business activity mostly automated and asynchronous.

items.title: Personal appointment + evening work
items.sharedDetail: Morning is open, but the afternoon and evening are spoken for. Keep the morning focused and calm.
items.detail: Use the open morning for work/admin priorities, then protect the personal block and evening shift.

items.title: Open leverage day
items.sharedDetail: Best open day of the week. Handle one meaningful money/work block, prep the Mexico-house list, and keep part of the day available for us.
items.detail: Revenue pipeline first, then the highest-impact portal reliability/UX work and Mexico-house preparation.

next30.title: Work, then Mexico house
next30.label: Sep 18–22
next30.sharedDetail: Work Friday and Saturday, then protect Sun–Tue for the Mexico house. Maintenance first, family/rest second, return Tuesday with a buffer.
next30.detail: Keep business work minimal during the protected house block unless something is genuinely time-sensitive.

next30.title: Four-day work run
next30.label: Sep 23–26
next30.sharedDetail: Four consecutive work days. Expect lower evening energy and plan recovery around them.
next30.detail: Use the run for income and career proof while automation keeps the business pipeline alive.

next30.title: Lighter calendar = transition window
next30.label: Sep 27 → early Oct
next30.sharedDetail: The calendar gets lighter. Use the opening deliberately: some family/home time, some better-work hunting, and a bounded 3DVR push rather than filling every day.
next30.detail: Turn successful paid technical work into a repeatable service and pursue higher-paying freelance/job opportunities while keeping Operator/CRM reliable.

next30.title: Make the portal useful to both of us
next30.label: By Oct 11
next30.sharedDetail: The portal should answer: what is Thomas working, when are we free, what home/family things need attention, and what is changing next.
next30.detail: Keep the shared page share-safe; sensitive client, health, credential, and internal operational details stay in protected systems.

next90.title: October — create breathing room
next90.label: Goal
next90.sharedDetail: Keep income steady while creating more control over the schedule and fewer chaotic work weeks.
next90.detail: Add at least one more paying client or strong recurring opportunity and replace weaker work where possible.

next90.title: November — make income more predictable
next90.label: Goal
next90.sharedDetail: Shift some income toward recurring work so each month does not start from zero.
next90.detail: Move toward maintenance, automation, website/server support, and narrow managed services with low support burden.

next90.title: December — protect what works
next90.label: Goal
next90.sharedDetail: Keep the work channels that actually help our life; stop feeding projects that only create more obligation.
next90.detail: Stop weak experiments and double down on the channels producing money, stability, and lower manual effort.

next90.title: Long arc
next90.label: Direction
next90.sharedDetail: Build toward more freedom over where we live, how much time we have together, and what kinds of work Thomas says yes to.
next90.detail: Dependable work stays the floor, better freelance work raises the rate, client technology work funds 3DVR, and 3DVR gradually performs more of its own work.

milestones.label: rest/family time protected in a normal week when possible
Mexico house care block protected this month
additional paying client or repeat engagement
independent revenue neighborhood to prove repeatability
shared portal plan both partners can understand quickly
fewer surprises and less reconstructing plans from messages
